page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system includes 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local NVMe storage and relies on network-attached storage, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Standard CPU and memory operations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark tests, consistently score in the bottom 10% to 25%, indicating weak general-purpose compute capabilities. Similarly, memory bandwidth and Redis database operations show poor to weak performance. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong results for machine learning tasks. Large language model (LLM) inference benchmarks place this instance in the top 10% for prompt processing and the top 25% for text generation when utilizing small (135M) and medium (7B) models.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is its low-tier CPU and memory performance paired with high-tier AI inference capabilities. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it serves as an entry-level GPU platform, offering access to hardware acceleration without the expense of high-end GPU architectures. It is optimized for lightweight machine learning inference, small-to-medium model execution, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering, rather than CPU-heavy database operations or high-throughput web serving.
